# JOURNAL — optimizer handover (append-only, whole run)

YOU (the optimizer) own this file. It is the running, accumulating handover across ALL iterations — accepted AND rejected — and it is NEVER reset. Each iteration you APPEND one new entry at the bottom (under the marker line); you do NOT edit or delete earlier entries. Read the whole journal before proposing, so you build on EVERY prior attempt (not just the last accepted one) and never re-test a refuted idea.

You CANNOT know your own gate result while you write — the harness scores you AFTER you stop and stamps a **RESULT** line (outcome + Δ + the EXACT tasks you broke/fixed) right below your entry. So do NOT write 'what worked' as a guess. To learn what actually worked, READ the framework RESULT lines of prior entries (and LEDGER.md): an entry whose RESULT says `rejected` with `broke={...}` tells you which specific edits to drop or redesign — its diff.patch is in ./prior_iterations/<id>/.

Append your entry for THIS iteration below the marker, using this shape (INTENT only — the framework appends the RESULT):

    ## Iteration <your candidate id> — <one-line headline of what you tried>
    - Changes I made (1 line per edit; name the file/tool + cluster it targets):
    - Per change, the EXPECTED effect + why it's safe (which failing task it should fix;
      why no passing task changes behavior):
    - Building on prior RESULTS: which prior entries' broke/fixed I used, and what I
      did NOT re-try because a prior RESULT showed it regressed (cite ids):
    - Refuted hypotheses (a prior RESULT proved this is NOT the fix — never re-test):
    - High-value clusters still NOT cracked (and the guard/tool designs already tried):
    - Plateau signal (are the last few RESULTs flat/negative? if so, which LEVER to switch
      to — e.g. a NEW composite tool instead of another guard, or prompt instead of code):
    - Focus next iteration:

## Iteration cand_0001 — teach the agent its code is re-run on hidden inputs (generalize, don't hardcode)
- Changes I made:
  - prompt.md: added a "WRITE GENERAL CODE" block — solution code is re-run on 2 hidden input
    files (same layout, different data) and must pass all 3; derive every value/count/index/date
    from the input at run time; never hardcode preview-observed literals; use `datetime.now()`
    for today/current-month; instruction-stated constants are fine. (Cluster 1: non-generalizing
    hardcoded literals — 56561, 34-5, and all 2/3 partials 267-18/250-20.)
  - prompt.md: added a "PRODUCE THE RESULT, NOT THE RECIPE" block — perform the macro/VBA/formula
    operation and write resulting values; never paste VBA/macro/script SOURCE into cells;
    formulas remain legal (grader recalculates). (Cluster 2: 269-44, 254-34 pasted VBA text.)
  - task_template.md: rewrote the interaction section into an ordered INSPECT → SOLVE(derive-from-
    input) → VERIFY(re-open, recompute one by hand, confirm nothing hardcoded) procedure, with
    verify as a precondition of finishing. (Cluster 3: stops at "Done" without real verify.)
- Expected effect + why safe: fixes the dominant class where code passes case 1 but fails 2/3 by
  baking in observed values. SAFE because the 51 passing tasks already generalize — 11 of them
  (37962, 49237, 50682, 2212, 31420, 32255, 35747, 37086, 44264, 45581, 54675) write Excel
  FORMULAS and pass 3/3, so I explicitly kept formulas legal and only banned hardcoding + pasting
  code-as-text, neither of which any passing task does. Template checklist doesn't change a
  correct trajectory's final artifact.
- Building on prior RESULTS: none — baseline only (LEDGER/JOURNAL/RUNMAP empty).
- Refuted hypotheses: none yet. NOTE for successors: do NOT reintroduce "prefer literal values
  over formulas" — evidence shows formulas are a winning, generalizing strategy here.
- High-value clusters still NOT cracked: color/theme-fill detection edge (267-18 case 3);
  fragile hand-written XML/pivot parsing (55912); spec-ambiguity tasks (45300). Designs not yet
  tried: worked example for robust color detection; a canonical openpyxl idiom snippet.
- Plateau signal: n/a (first iteration).
- Focus next iteration: if accepted, measure which 2/3-partials flipped to 3/3; then target the
  color-detection and interpretation-ambiguity clusters with worked examples. If REJECTED, the
  generalization block is likely still right but check whether the template rewrite added turns
  that timed out any passing task — if so, keep the prompt.md blocks and revert the template.

> **RESULT (framework, objective):** ACCEPTED (new champion) · val=0.582 Δ=+0.022 · fixed={254-34, 267-18, 41410, 45300, 48588, 56561} · broke={31420, 347-49, 42930, 50631}.
